decisions.reason: As a 2023 launch with its own page and a close fit to the firm's core space camera business, management is likely to continue backing it because investment and public commitment are already substantial and weak signals can still be read as temporary.
This product line has strong public visibility, multiple models, and a visible mission success in 2024, so escalation of commitment and positive validation make withdrawal very unlikely.
The sensor suite builds on the established offer, remains prominently presented, and fits the firm's stated direction, so management would be inclined to persist unless failure became much clearer.

The miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR sensor has weaker market visibility than the page-based products, but its strategic relevance to compact future spacecraft systems and the firm's R&D-oriented culture still favor continuation.

As a newly launched 2024 radiation-hard camera line with several models and its own page, it represents fresh investment and a visible strategic commitment that management would be reluctant to reverse quickly.

Although only mentioned on the website and likely more niche, it is very new, closely related to the firm's space-navigation heritage, and management can still plausibly attribute any slow uptake to long space-sector adoption cycles rather than product failure.
